drug_class: Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI), Type B selective

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Serotonergic effects combined with MAOI activity increase serotonin syndrome risk

avoid_supplements.name: 5-HTP
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Increased serotonin levels with MAOI inhibition causes serotonin syndrome risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid; may cause hypertensive crisis or serotonin syndrome

avoid_supplements.name: L-Tryptophan
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Serotonin precursor with MAOI leads to excessive serotonin accumulation

avoid_supplements.name: SAMe (S-adenosyl methionine)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Serotonergic activity potentiated by MAOI effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use with caution under medical supervision

avoid_supplements.name: Ginseng
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Stimulant properties with MAOI may cause hypertensive crisis

avoid_supplements.name: Yohimbine
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Alpha-adrenergic stimulation combined with MAOI increases hypertension risk

caution_supplements.name: Tyrosine (L-Tyrosine)
caution_supplements.mechanism: At high doses, may increase catecholamine synthesis with MAOI activity
caution_supplements.action: Use normal dietary amounts; avoid supplemental megadoses

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium
caution_supplements.mechanism: No direct interaction but may enhance CNS effects

avoid_foods.name: Aged cheeses (cheddar, blue, Parmesan, brie)
avoid_foods.mechanism: High tyramine content with MAOI causes tyramine pressor effect and hypertensive crisis
avoid_foods.action: Strictly avoid; risk of severe hypertension and intracranial hemorrhage

avoid_foods.name: Cured/processed meats (salami, pepperoni, bacon, sausage)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Tyramine accumulation from preservation combined with MAO-B inhibition

avoid_foods.name: Fermented soy products (miso, soy sauce, tempeh)
avoid_foods.mechanism: High tyramine from fermentation with MAOI blockade

avoid_foods.name: Overripe or spoiled bananas
avoid_foods.mechanism: Tyramine increases with ripening and bacterial decomposition
avoid_foods.action: Avoid very ripe bananas; fresh ripe bananas in moderation acceptable

avoid_foods.name: Broad beans (fava beans)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Naturally high dopamine and tyramine content

caution_foods.name: Soy milk and tofu (non-fermented)
caution_foods.mechanism: Lower tyramine than fermented soy but contains some biogenic amines

caution_foods.name: Avocados
caution_foods.mechanism: Contains small amounts of tyramine; variable ripeness affects content
caution_foods.action: Limit to 1 per week or use occasionally if well-tolerated

caution_foods.name: Spinach, tomatoes
caution_foods.mechanism: Trace to minimal tyramine levels in fresh produce
caution_foods.action: Generally safe in normal dietary quantities

caution_foods.name: Caffeine
caution_foods.mechanism: May potentiate sympathomimetic effects; theoretical hypertension risk
caution_foods.action: Limit intake; monitor blood pressure response

caution_foods.name: Chocolate
caution_foods.mechanism: Contains tyramine and phenylethylamine in small amounts
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption; excessive amounts best avoided

monitoring_notes: At therapeutic doses of 5-10 mg daily, selegiline shows selective MAO-B inhibition with reduced tyramine interactions compared to non-selective MAOIs, but dietary restrictions still apply, especially at higher doses. Monitor for hypertensive crisis (sudden severe headache, chest pain, vision changes) and serotonin syndrome symptoms (agitation, tremor, hyperthermia, rigidity); counsel patients thoroughly on tyramine-restricted diet.
